title: Challenge For Someone
author: Arbetraryday
selftext:
For someone that isn't worried about token usage (I am). 

I am curious what would happen if you put together a small spec to build the 'ideal game' based on web research. 

Hook up the Blender MCP and MCP for whichever engine you prefer. Then let the agents rip. 

I think the spec should contain technical stack and how to decide what to do/how to test/playability/planning. 

If someone is serious, happy to help build the prompt.

comments.author: Charming_You_25
comments.body: In my experience, AI has some issues with 3-D, and it might get stuck if left unattended for too long. It’s polishing ability based on a photo where you take a screenshot of what you currently have and then run it through image generation to make it polished and then have the AI automatically implement it. It will get pretty far but if looping for long enough, it will miss details and caused regressions it won’t catch.

replies.author: Arbetraryday
replies.body:
I am right there with you. I am 500+ prompts into my game with plenty of screenshot and created/downloaded(purchased) assets. 

I think the real challenge here is two sided. 1) What content can I add to a design doc to get a legit outcome. 
2) Based on a refined web research, what does an agent conclude is the ideal game. 

I think it would be an interesting experiment to see just how far a well made design doc could go. For someone who has seen tribulation with ai game dev, you could be alot more specific based on the snags you ran into. 

I don't expect a perfect game to come out of this, but perhaps we get another meme of AI trying to do things on it's own, or find some hidden knowledge. The "Wow, I didn't realize the AI would do that"

In a recent video I saw. They drew a comparison of VFX artists vs. AI. And the truth of the matter was, AI does a bad job at adhering to creative control. But does surprisingly well when it isn't required to adhere to a human vision. So that sparked this idea. Give the agents creative freedom with a derived goal based on research. Set the guarrails and see what happens. 

All that being said. I completely agree with your feedback, from my experience

replies.author: Charming_You_25
replies.body: I also think even with the web research AI isn’t creative enough necessarily to come up with a game without you, providing it a structure that produces the type of game you want to make. If you wanted to clone another game, it would be great for that.

comments.author: proximalcoast
comments.body:
I’m on the x20 plan. I’ve posted about this concept in the past, but this would go well beyond token wasting.

and i love using tokens (last week):

https://preview.redd.it/nq3pp6690sjh1.jpeg?width=222&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=b5a25aa3b9188d4ca2c34ba8d9c5de9cc962dcb6

  
The problem is what “good” actually is. AI has no idea, even when you tell it. It took a huge amount of tokens and time to make some reasonable walls for my game.

General outline:

Regular chat for concept art

Load concept art, generate particular prompt for making it, subagent loops, texture, expected topology, uv maps, etc.

Execute via codex

ACTUALLY GET BLENDER MCP TO BE USED (it’s so bad at this, makes .py files constantly, and falls back to it all the time, even post prompt/steer)

Subagents will eventually give up on quality, and won’t compare to the concept art, the higher order agent sometimes catches it, probably about 1 in 4 do

So letting it go ad-hoc is white hot garbage… however once you do get something good (first flat wall took a really long time, first outset long took slightly less, the other variants were non-guided). Just that alone was probably 300M-400M tokens. 

I think MAYBE it would be possible if the game was super small, but it’s not gonna have the desired polish. The AI devil is in the details.

comments.author: shiftpgdn
comments.body: It will fail because it can't "understand" un-textured 3d objects.

comments.author: zenmatrix83
comments.body: I have a loop prompt thats way too long to past here, it boostraps any projects, and it looks for mcp servers or apis for whatever. I just create a [spec.md](http://spec.md) file and a [loop.md](http://loop.md) file and run /loop.md  and it boostraps a project with agents, some are just sonnect or haiku , with opus being the driver. It creates a whole structure project and doest testing design and alot of other things, but has critera for a hard stop where I review. I let it run in on a second screen while I do stuff now and it runs for awhile. I have the x20 plan and it works basically non stop, ever 15-45 mins as the loops sometime wait a bit because sub agents finish quickly.

replies.author: zenmatrix83
replies.body: I have it take screenshots with headless godot and or the browser depending on what I'm doing and review those and then I check them also once in awhile and send feedback, and then custom edit anything the models can't do
